title: Taylor approximation of the Gaussian exponential
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, let $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be a continuous real-linear map, and let $p\in[0,\infty]$ satisfy $p<\infty$. Under standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$ on $\mathbb R^n$, the $L^p$ quasi-norm of the error between $e^{L(x)}$ and its degree-$(k-1)$ Taylor polynomial tends to zero as $k\to\infty$; explicitly, $\|e^{L(\cdot)}-\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}L(\cdot)^m/m!\|_{L^p(\gamma_n)}\to0$.
hypotheses_covered: $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ is continuous and real-linear
